summary: Over the 14-day analysis period, time-in-range (70–180 mg/dL) averaged 86.0% with a standard deviation of 39.7 mg/dL. Time above range was 8.9% and time below range was 5.1%, with recorded glucose extremes dipping into the 40s mg/dL overnight and early morning. The active AAPS profile features a flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, variable carb ratios, and a 10-hour DIA, operating under Oref1 closed-loop automation with SMB and UAM enabled. The dataset contains no recorded carbohydrate treatment entries, indicating that meals are unannounced or unlogged, relying entirely on UAM and reactive micro-bolusing to manage postprandial glycemic excursions.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is 98.7% across 3,995 entries with a 5-minute cadence and good data quality status. Minor gaps exist, with the largest being 65 minutes.
analysis_steps.evidence: Total entries: 3995; coverage percent: 98.7%; gap count: 10; largest gap: 65.0 minutes.

analysis_steps.findings: Strong overall time in range (86.0%), but significant time below range (5.1%) with glucose dropping to 41-42 mg/dL on multiple days, imposing a strict safety constraint against aggressive insulin increases.
analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%, glucose extremes down to 41 mg/dL on Aug 13, 14, and 21.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of declared meal carb entries limits direct postprandial attribution.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight glucose averages 90-105 mg/dL with notable time below range (up to 18.5% at hour 0-1 local time), indicating slight over-delivery or high sensitivity during fasting states. Afternoon hours show elevated averages up to 162.8 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local glucose shows overnight dips into 90s and afternoon peaks up to 162.8 mg/dL (hour 16).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unannounced meals confound the separation of basal vs postprandial effects.

analysis_steps.findings: The profile uses a single flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, variable CR segments, and a 10-hour DIA. Oref1 dynamic sensitivity is actively adjusting delivery, compensating for the flat ISF.
analysis_steps.evidence: ISF 56 mg/dL/U flat, CR segments 10.5-13.2 g/U, DIA 10 hours, dynamic sensitivity enabled at 70%.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of tagged meal data prevents independent verification of CR segments.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled with smb_always_enabled=true, allowing microbolusing without declared COB. This successfully manages unannounced meals but shifts the entire postprandial burden onto closed-loop automation.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No declared carbohydrate entries to evaluate automated response against known meal sizes.

analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF is active (70% adjustment factor) while Autosens is disabled. Max IOB is set to 25 U, which is very high relative to daily insulin needs (~20 U/day) and poses a safety risk if runaway stacking occurs.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled=false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true (70%), max_iob_units=25 U, total daily insulin ~20 U.

analysis_steps.findings: Meals are unannounced or unlogged in Nightscout. Oref1 relies entirely on UAM and SMB to catch postprandial rises, leading to avoidable afternoon peaks before automation reacts.
analysis_steps.evidence: Total carbs in treatment summary is 0.0g; afternoon glucose averages peak at 162.8 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete absence of meal timing and carbohydrate quantity data.

analysis_steps.findings: No extended carb or e-carb entries exist in the dataset. The carb absorption model uses a 7-hour maximum absorption window and minimum 5m carb impact of 8 mg/dL/5 min.
analysis_steps.evidence: average_extended_carb_duration_min is null, carb_treatment_entries is empty.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No e-carb or extended carb utilization to assess.

analysis_steps.findings: Evidence supports keeping current profile and automation settings stable while initiating meal logging and verifying overnight basal stability. Changing dependent insulin parameters simultaneously is contraindicated due to hypoglycemia risk.
analysis_steps.evidence: 86% TIR, 5.1% TBR with lows in 40s, 0g logged carbs, active Oref1 dynamic sensitivity.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of declared meal data limits parameter optimization.

strengths: High time-in-range of 86.0% over 14 days demonstrating generally effective closed-loop control.
Excellent CGM data quality (98.7% coverage) with robust device status and telemetry logging.
Active Oref1 automation with dynamic ISF and UAM successfully handles unannounced meals without catastrophic hyperglycemia.
issues: Time below range of 5.1% with multiple glucose readings dipping into the 40s mg/dL overnight and early morning.
Total absence of declared meal carbohydrate entries (0g logged), forcing the system to rely entirely on reactive UAM and SMB.
Afternoon postprandial peaks exceeding 160 mg/dL on average due to the lack of proactive prebolusing or meal announcements.

recommendations.title: Verify Overnight Basal and Fasting Stability
recommendations.description: Overnight glucose dips into the 40s and 50s mg/dL (e.g., 18.5% time below range at hour 0 local time) suggest that early-night basal rates (0.6 U/h from 00:00) may be slightly too high during periods of high insulin sensitivity. Keep settings unchanged for now while monitoring overnight trends closely.

suggested_change.rationale: Withhold basal adjustments until meal logging provides a clear baseline, mitigating hypoglycemia risk.

recommendations.title: Evaluate Max IOB Safety Limit
recommendations.description: Max IOB is set to 25 U, which is exceptionally high relative to total daily insulin (~20 U/day). While it prevents artificial throttling during highs, consider evaluating whether a lower ceiling is safer once meal logging is established.

suggested_change.rationale: Assess runaway SMB stacking risk against current total daily dose.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Overall time in range is strong at 86.0%, and closed-loop automation (Oref1 with dynamic sensitivity) is actively managing variability. Given the presence of overnight hypoglycemia (5.1% TBR with lows in the 40s) and unannounced meals, changing static profile baselines or ISF without meal data introduces unwarranted instability.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Record exact meal times and carbohydrate amounts for at least 3 consecutive days to evaluate postprandial excursions and assess whether dynamic sensitivity is adequately compensating for the flat ISF.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile settings unchanged and initiate consistent meal logging to improve automation responsiveness.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Introduce consistent logging of meal carbohydrates paired with a modest 15-20 minute prebolus or temporary target reduction before meals. This allows Oref1 to manage postprandial glycemic rises proactively rather than relying entirely on reactive UAM micro-bolusing.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: In the complete absence of declared meal carbohydrate entries (0g logged), closed-loop automation must rely entirely on UAM and SMB. This reactive posture leads to avoidable postprandial peaks (afternoon averages of 140-162 mg/dL) and increases the risk of stacking.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record exact meal times and carbohydrate amounts for at least 3 consecutive days to evaluate true CR accuracy and separate unannounced meal impact from basal/ISF drift.

exceptions.suggestion: Monitor overnight glucose closely between 00:00 and 05:00 local time where time below range reaches 18.5% in some hourly bins.
exceptions.rationale: Fasting overnight windows exhibit downward drift due to high insulin sensitivity interacting with automated micro-boluses.

exceptions.suggestion: Review meal composition for high fat/protein content if postprandial elevations persist after initiating meal logging.
exceptions.rationale: Delayed absorption can outpace standard UAM detection, resulting in temporary hyperglycemia.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Begin logging all meal times and carbohydrate amounts in Nightscout for 3 consecutive days without changing any profile or automation settings.
Step 2: Review the resulting meal response windows to assess whether postprandial peaks decrease with proactive logging and prebolusing.
Step 3: Evaluate overnight CGM trends to verify whether fasting stability improves once unannounced meal noise is removed.
Step 4: Consult the clinical care team before making any adjustments to basal rates, ISF, or CR segments.
education: Unannounced meals force closed-loop systems to rely on rate-of-change detection (UAM), which inherently lags behind actual digestion and causes postprandial glucose spikes.
Dynamic ISF adjusts insulin sensitivity in real-time based on glucose behavior, helping compensate for a static, flat profile ISF during changing insulin resistance states.
Max IOB limits control how much insulin the automated loop can deliver above baseline, balancing the need to correct highs against the risk of insulin stacking and severe hypoglycemia.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice.
Given recorded nocturnal glucose values in the 40s mg/dL, any proposed increase in insulin delivery or sensitivity must be approached with extreme caution.
